## What was inherited, and what was re-verified

The batch's first container died at 23:22 UTC on 2026-09-18, 25 minutes in.  One commit
was on the branch, `7e666704`: the failing test, the four probes `r2a`, `r2b`, `r2c`,
`r2e`, and `probes/junit-before.out`.  The worktree also held the uncommitted edit to
`CodeGen.java` and `FIntLiteral.java`, a draft of this report, and `tmp/` logs whose last
line showed `library_tests/Integer.test` starting and never finishing.

Everything was re-run rather than read off those logs: the rung's own test (`OK (2 tests)`,
`probes/junit-after.out`, re-taken 23:33), every probe both ways (the `.after` files; phase
B had never reached them), and `Integer.test`, which is the run that had been cut off.  The
built classes were checked against the sources before trusting them:
`javap -c` on `build/.../codegen/CodeGen.class` shows `bipush 31` and `bipush 63` at the
two branch tests, and on `build/.../runtimeValues/FIntLiteral.class` shows `asNN64` reading
`largerVal` through `BigInteger`.

Five probes are new in this session: `r2d`, `r2f` (two diagnostics the repair restores),
`r2g`, `r2h` (what the interpreter does with the idiom the repair uncovers) and `r2i` (the
legal spelling of the two values that idiom was reaching for).

=== 165,190 ===
reading of a numeral.

`probes/r2g` and `probes/r2h` settle it: the interpreter has always refused the idiom —
`a: ZZ32 = 8000'0000_16` is "RHS expression type Long is not assignable to LHS type ZZ32",
and `a: ZZ64 = 8000'0000'0000'0000_16` is the same for `BigNum`.  So these are not correct
programs the repair broke.  They are programs the language does not accept, which the
compile path accepted only because the wrap turned them into something else, and on which
the two paths now **agree**.  The repair reduces the divergence between `walk` and the
compiled run; it does not create any.

The complete blast radius was measured rather than guessed: every numeral in the corpora
and the libraries whose value has bit length exactly 32 or exactly 64 was enumerated by
value, in every radix (`probes/boundary-numerals.txt`).  Eighteen of those lines are on the
compile path.  Twelve are in range for their annotated type (`CompilerLibrary.fss:574,576`
`NN32_MAX` and `NN64_MAX`, `ShiftTest.fss:32,33`, `NN32.fss:43,46`, `NN64.fss:45,46,48`,
`ZZ.fss:44`, `AverageTest.fss:118`, `ShiftTest2.fss:194`) and are now correct where they had
been right only by the wrap's accident.  Six are out of range: the five repaired here
(`CompilerLibrary.fss:569,571`, `Integer3.fss:46`, `Integer4.fss:46`,
`IntegerChoose2.fss:114`) and `library_tests/ChooseTest3.fss:125`, which is in no `.test`
file (`LibraryJUTest.java:36` sweeps `.test` files only), so it is not gated and is left for
the record rather than edited unverified.  The remaining lines the enumeration shows are in
the interpreter-only libraries `Library/QuickCheck.fss` and `Library/Random.fss`, which are
not part of the compile-path prelude, in `ProjectFortress/tests/`, whose two hits are
untyped comparisons of the same numeral to itself (`NumeralTest.fss:44-45`) and numerals
inside string literals, and in this rung's own test.

# R2 record lines

## For `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md`

Under **Execution model**, after the line on the code generator lowering every type to a
JVM reference type:

- **A numeral's value reaches the compiled world intact as of the repair batch of 2026-09-18.** `CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr` chose the numeral's representation by `BigInteger.bitLength()` against `<= 32` and `<= 64`; `bitLength()` counts no sign bit, so a non-negative numeral of bit length exactly 32 or exactly 64 was truncated into a signed slot and arrived wrapped negative — `4294967295` and `18446744073709551615` both became `-1`, against `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-86` (a numeral of digits has the value of its digits in radix ten, with nothing bounding it) and `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:368-370,398-401` (wrapping and saturating have their own operator spellings and "operations on type $\mathbb{Z}$ never need to wrap or saturate"). The bounds are now `<= 31` and `<= 63`, exact for both signs, and `FIntLiteral.asNN64` reads the decimal string a numeral of bit length 64 now keeps. Where the compiled run contradicted `walk` in silence it now agrees with it: `4294967295` at `ZZ` prints `4294967295` on both paths, and `a = 4294967295; b = 1; println (a + b)` prints `4294967296` on both (ledger row 317, `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/REPORT.md`).
- **A radix numeral is a natural number, not a bit pattern, and the compile path was the only place that pretended otherwise.** `literals.tex:104-108` gives a radix numeral the type `NaturalNumeralWithExplicitRadix[[n,r,v]]` over the value of its digits in radix $r$, so `8000'0000_16` is $2^{31}$ and `A0000000_16` is $2684354560$; the interpreter has always refused such a numeral at a signed type ("RHS expression type Long is not assignable to LHS type ZZ32"), and the compile path accepted it only because the wrap turned it into something else. Five sites in the tree relied on that: `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:569,571` (`ZZ32_MIN`, `ZZ64_MIN`), `library_tests/Integer3.fss:46` and `Integer4.fss:46` (`twiceHuge`), and `library_tests/IntegerChoose2.fss:114` with its ungated twin `ChooseTest3.fss:125`. The first four are repaired value-for-value; the fifth was not only illegal but was exercising `i = -1257966796` instead of the $\sqrt{2^{63}}$ boundary its own comment names.
- Every numeral in the corpora and the libraries whose value has bit length exactly 32 or exactly 64 is enumerated, by value and in every radix, at `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/boundary-numerals.txt`; eighteen of the enumerated lines are on the compile path, twelve of them in range for their annotated type and right until now only by the wrap's accident. A decimal-only grep misses the radix-16 half, which is where four of the five out-of-range sites were, and where the `Integer.test` failures came from.

content.content: **The inherited concurrent test's own comment was wrong about the gate, and my correction of it was wrong in the other direction.** It had said that at the thread count "every gate target uses" the program passes whether or not the implementation is correct, citing the review's `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`; that pin is in the `testSystem` shards only (`build.xml:1184`), which run `SystemJUTest` and not `compiler_tests`. So far so good, and the chain I put in its place is right as far as it goes: the target that runs `compiler_tests` is `CompilerJUTest` under the `fastTrack` macro (`build.xml:927-953`), which sets `FORTRESS_CACHES` and no thread count and no `newenvironment`, so the forked JUnit JVM inherits the shell; the harness runs each program in a further subprocess that inherits again (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:480-486`); and `FortressExecutable.getNumThreads` falls back to the processor count or `floor(n/2)` (`:37-44`). What I missed is the first line of that method: the fallback applies **only when `FORTRESS_THREADS` is unset**, and `experiment/env.sh:6` exports `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`, which the batch brief tells every agent to source and which `explorations/coordinator/iteration-cost.md:126` records as the setting of every run in the climb. In the gate as this project actually runs it there is one worker, and `AtomicTopLevelVar` passes vacuously there: measured on the base tree, `BASE run AtomicTopLevelVar THREADS=1 :: PASS` (`probes/skeptic/skeptic-basetree.txt`). I had to `unset FORTRESS_THREADS` in my own capture script (`tmp/final-capture.sh:40`) to get the rows I then called "the thread count the gate actually uses". The residual limitation is therefore not only a machine whose `availableProcessors` is 1 or 3; it is any shell that sourced the project's own env file. `MutableTopLevelVarInLoop` fails at one thread and is what carries the gate; the concurrent test is worth keeping as the check that the invariant holds under real contention, and the test's own comment now says all of this.

files: explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/ (77 probe sources and captures, incl. probes/skeptic/)
explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/ (128 probe sources and captures, incl. the eight .out files added with git add -f)

conflicts: None. R1's net change (git diff 49ee5e91...wip/repair-r1-atomic-static, 5374 lines, 139 paths) applied with `git apply --3way --index` with no rejected hunk; the applied tree is identical to the branch outside the coordinator files main has moved ahead on (`git diff --stat wip/repair-r1-atomic-static -- ProjectFortress explorations/compile-ladder` empty).
None. R2's net change (2625 lines, 131 paths) applied the same way with no rejected hunk, on top of R1.

The one file both rungs touch, CodeGen.java, took both sets of hunks without a conflict: R1's at :1858, :4647, :4756, :4812 and :5874-5949 (64 lines), R2's at :3873-3886 (7 lines). Verified three ways after the second apply: the combined change is 71 lines (64+7); the literal branch reads `bitLength() <= 31` and `<= 63`; R1's addTopLevelVarBinding is still present. No hand resolution was needed.
correctionsClosed: R1/1 regression of finding 1 (atomic on an object- or trait-typed top-level variable must not crash) - CLOSED ON THE BRANCH (95647b4d), verified here in the applied tree: `grep -n 'debug(' ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/*.java` leaves no unguarded call site (Transaction.java:128,140,162,166,180,185,198,203,227,232,240,249,265,274 and BaseTask.java:183,186,193,195,207,234,242,248,258 all carry `if (debug)`); MutableFValue.toString no longer dereferences the payload through asString (MutableFValue.java:38-39, now `String.valueOf(value)`); both-tree probes are at probes/failure-object-type-before-guard.txt and probes/pass-after-guard.txt, and the case is gated by compiler_tests/AtomicTopLevelObjectVar, whose object type declares no asString.

R1/2 ledger row for finding 2 (atomic in a `do ... also` arm) - CLOSED ON THE BRANCH; folded here as ledger row 322, naming CodeGen.java:4733-4741 and :1735-1753, the disassembly in probes/skeptic/sk13-verifyerror.txt, the probes both ways and the ALOAD/SWAP fix.

R1/3 ledger row against the interpreter for finding 4 (SK5InitFwd) - CLOSED ON THE BRANCH; folded here as ledger row 323, with the SK26InitFwdImmutable control that narrows it to a later *mutable* variable.

R1/4 FACTS line on compiler_tests and concurrency qualified - CLOSED ON THE BRANCH; the folded FACTS bullet cites experiment/env.sh:6, iteration-cost.md:126 and the measured `BASE run AtomicTopLevelVar THREADS=1 :: PASS`, and REPORT.md:24 states the residual limitation as "any shell that sourced the project's own env file", not only availableProcessors 1 or 3.
R1/5 the bound from finding 2 added to the rung's FACTS line - CLOSED ON THE BRANCH; the folded bullet carries "**The bound**: this is `atomic` in a function body or a loop body" with row 322.

R1/6 REPORT.md "eleven programs" is ten - CLOSED ON THE BRANCH (REPORT.md:151: ten programs named by atomicTest.test plus the ungated nestedTransactions3, "22 runs, of which 20 are gated programs and 2 are the ungated eleventh").
R1/7 REPORT.md "Eighteen .test files" is sixteen - CLOSED ON THE BRANCH (REPORT.md:124 now reads sixteen at 49ee5e91 and sixteen at HEAD, with eighteen attributed to the inherited commit 029b7454).

R1/8 record.md harness line also handles `_equals` - CLOSED ON THE BRANCH; the folded FACTS bullet lists six checks including `_equals` at FileTests.java:190. I re-verified :190 and the default at :266-272 in the tree.
R1/9 the cost sentence - CLOSED ON THE BRANCH (REPORT.md:278 states it in two states, naming Transaction.java:162,166,227, :232, :249, the 40,000 transactions and row 302's ~34% of a 156x gap).

R1/10 which corpora the competing-declaration grep covered - CLOSED ON THE BRANCH (REPORT.md:169 distinguishes the ladder-subset grep over ProjectFortress/tests/ from the name grep over all five corpora, and cites the three other corpora from the skeptic's finding 5).

R1/11 the initialization.tex derivation reworded as permissive - CLOSED ON THE BRANCH (REPORT.md:182: initialization.tex:15-17,29-30 "declines to forbid a forward reference rather than licensing one", with variables.tex:122-123 as the prescriptive citation).

R1/12 REPORT.md's Transaction.java payload-type citation off by one - CLOSED HERE. Replaced with the complete verified set (`grep -n '\bAny\b'`): :20,27-28,112-113,121-122,144,152,154,160,182,184,199,201-202,226,246,248,255,257-258,270,272 - a superset of the thirteen positions the skeptic named, agreeing with each. A note under the block records the correction. While checking the same block I found and fixed one further wrong entry in it: MutableFValue.java was cited at :42, the file's closing brace, where the toString change is at :38-39. I did not re-audit the codegen ranges in that block: the skeptic checked them and some are method ranges rather than hunk ranges.

R1/13 the inference stated as fact about AtomicTopLevelObjectVar's local half - CLOSED HERE. REPORT.md now says it is an inference, from SK20LocalTrait (a trait-typed local, run on the base tree) together with LocalMutableVar's having always routed through TXWrite, and that the test's recorded failure is against the pre-guard landed tree and does not rest on the claim. JUDGE.md, which carried the claim, is left as the judge wrote it.

R1/14 ledger row 324 marked derived rather than measured - CLOSED HERE. The claim column now says the wrong answer is measured and the mechanism is derived from CodeGen.java:1735,1738 and Transaction.java:144-149,159-168, and names what a probe would still confirm. The skeptic's worth-adding items are in too: SQ7ObjThrow extends the measurement to an object type, and BaseTask.java:83-86 explains why a second implicit thread sees the stale value (SQ6OrphanTx); both probes are added to the row's reproducer column.

R2/1 commit the eight captured .out files - CLOSED HERE. Copied from /home/user/fortress-r2 and added with `git add -f` under their own names, so the citations in REPORT.md and record.md resolve: probes/junit-before.out (the recorded failure, `FAIL: ZZ from the 32-bit numeral: -1 should be 4294967295`), junit-after.out, junit-codegen-only.out, junit-repaired.out, junit-final.out (`OK (2 tests)`) and integer-test-before/after/repaired.out. Renaming was the other option and was rejected because it would dangle every citation. .gitignore is unchanged; `git ls-files` on the probes directory now lists all eight.

R2/2 the p37 claim corrected in all three places and the row it hides opened - CLOSED HERE. record.md's row-317 amendment and its handover paragraph now drop p37 from the agreeing list and state what it does; REPORT.md's "it does not create any [divergence]" is replaced by the measured exception, and its divergence table carries a p37 row. New ledger row 328: IntLiteral comparison is performed at ZZ64 (CompilerBuiltin.fss:837-842, verified in the tree), FIntLiteral.asZZ64 raises for a string-carried numeral (:74-77, message at :63-65), literals.tex:83-86 requires false, and the fix is comparison in BigInteger as simpleIntLiteralArith.java:26-27 already does. I confirmed the divergence from the committed captures: p37.walk.skeptic prints three false lines, p37.compiled.skeptic raises `Not in range for ZZ64: 18446744073709551615`; p37a agrees both ways.

R2/3 which recorded state was inherited - CLOSED HERE. REPORT.md's "What was inherited, and what was re-verified" now names the exception: probes/junit-codegen-only.out and the four r2*.compiled.codegen-only outputs are dated 23:17, were produced by the first container's tmp/phaseA.sh (which reverted FIntLiteral.java with git checkout, rebuilt and measured), were committed in a6c0f031 by the second session and were not re-taken; the fact they carry is also readable from the pre-image, which is how the skeptic confirmed it.

R2/4 the loud-to-quiet transition recorded - CLOSED HERE. A new "## The failure-mode question" section in REPORT.md and a new FACTS bullet: FIntLiteral.asNN64 threw for every string-carried numeral before the rung, simpleIntLiteralArith.fromBigInteger sends every IntLiteral arithmetic result of bit length >= 64 to the string branch (:31-32, verified), so `x = 9223372036854775807; n: NN64 = x + x + 1` went from `Error: Not in range for NN64: 18446744073709551615` to the value 2^64-1 printed as -1 (probes/skeptic/s3.fss, s3.compiled; walk refuses the coercion, s3.walk). The value is specification-correct, the error that named the true value is gone while the rendering is wrong, and it is tied to row 326 (R2's proposed 320) in both directions.

Both rungs are on main as one clean local commit each, in order R1 (42d51c47) then R2 (6a63980b), 142 files each. Nothing is merged: `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms neither wip branch is an ancestor of HEAD. Nothing was pushed. The tree is clean and .gitignore is untouched.

No conflict was met. Both net changes applied with `git apply --3way --index` with no rejected hunk, including in CodeGen.java, which both rungs edit about 2,000 lines apart; the combined 71-line change equals R1's 64 plus R2's 7, and I read both regions afterwards to confirm neither lost a hunk.

All 14 of R1's required corrections and all 4 of R2's are closed. Eleven of R1's were closed on the branch in its repair round; I re-verified each against the tree rather than the report (the debug guards by grep over runtimeSystem/*.java, FileTests.java:190 and :266-272, the corpus counts, the reworded initialization.tex derivation) and closed the three the second skeptic left open. All four of R2's were open; I closed them, which included opening the fourth new ledger row the p37 misreport had hidden.

The record is folded in three places. FACTS.md: ten bullets at the end of "The compile-path ladder baseline", R1's five then R2's five. The gap ledger: four appends to existing rows (59, 70, 302, and row 317's amendment, whose stale CompilerBuiltin.fss:557 citation is corrected to :562 -- verified, :557 is the comment above ceilingAverage) and ten new rows, 319-324 for R1 and 325-328 for R2. No row was renumbered, moved or deleted; the row count goes 363 to 373 and every new and amended row has the table's eight columns. The handover: two paragraphs in "Where the work stands".

Five decisions, each with its alternative. (1) Row numbering: R1 was folded first and took the 319-324 it proposed, so R2's proposed 319, 320 and 321 became 325, 326 and 327 and its fourth row 328. The alternative was to renumber R1. R2's record.md now carries a note stating the mapping, because its SKEPTIC.md cites the proposed numbers. (2) FACTS placement: both rungs' bullets went under "The compile-path ladder baseline" per the gather brief, although R2's record.md asked for "Execution model"; one placement is auditable and the repair rungs belong with the eight they repair. A note in R2's record.md records where they actually went. (3) R2's four rows arrived as prose, not table rows, so I transformed them into the ledger's eight columns; for the two rows whose prose gave no specification clause (326, the signed NN rendering, and 327, the ungated ChooseTest3) I put an em dash rather than assert a silence I had not verified. (4) The handover paragraphs say the rung is landed on main as a commit composed at the gather stage and that the branch is not its parent; pasting "is on wip/..." verbatim would have been stale the moment it landed. No `<short hash>` placeholder was needed: neither record asks for one. (5) The pre-existing FACTS bullet on the literal wrap (now line 99) would have read as current, so I appended one clause marking it repaired by R2 and pointing at the entries below; it is otherwise unchanged.

Three things the next stage should know. No build and no gate was run here, per the brief; a clean textual apply is not a compile, and the pair is R1 and R2's only joint test. R2's skeptic left three recommended-not-required items unclosed, and they stay open: the CHOOSE measurement for row 327 with the two interpreter rows it suggests (probes/skeptic/s7, s8, s9, s10), two more assertions in IntLiteralWrapRepairR2.fss for the negative half of "exact for both signs", and probes/run-probes.sh, which sources the untracked /home/user/fortress-r2/tmp/r2env.sh and so will not run for the next reader. FACTS.md's "## The ledger" bullet still says 309 rows as of 2026-09-16; it is dated, so it is stale rather than wrong, and updating it was outside this stage.
